key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train agent systems that use real-world, multi-turn inference harnesses end-to-end, instead of treating those harnesses as untouchable inference-only wrappers. In simple terms: it bridges the gap between powerful agent runtimes and open-source training stacks.
problem_solved: Current RL/SFT frameworks struggle to represent stateful, multi-process harness inference like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenClaw. This limits end-to-end training of harness-native agents across diverse environments and external tools.
method: Provides an open-source framework designed specifically for harness-based agent training.
Supports end-to-end training of agents that operate through stateful, multi-turn inference harnesses.
Enables training across diverse environments while preserving the agent’s real execution/inference loop.
impact: This matters because practitioners can now train agents in the same harness they will use at deployment, reducing mismatch between training and real use. It opens the door to more practical, scalable, and reproducible development of tool-using AI agents.

paper_title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
paper_authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
